title: What If a Crater in Siberia Kept Growing Every Year?

scenes.text: What if the ground itself kept collapsing? In Siberia, one hole grows every single year.
It is called the Batagaika megaslump, and it was only about 790 meters wide in 2014.
By 2023 it was about 990 meters wide, nearly a kilometer, and still opening.
Its headwall retreats roughly 12 meters a year, and it sheds about a million cubic meters of ice and soil.
The walls expose permafrost up to about 650,000 years old, by one estimate.
Scientists say the digging down is nearly done, but it keeps eating sideways as the Arctic warms.

description:
What if the ground itself kept collapsing?
Siberia's Batagaika megaslump grew from about 790 to 990 meters wide in nine years and exposes permafrost up to 650,000 years old.
